releaseSource.integrity: Every deployed file was read from git HEAD and byte-checked against its git tree entry before upload. Uncommitted artifacts were excluded.

assertions.observation: The deployed top-level document exposed the exact state- and selection-scoped catalog through the native client without connector setup.
Native inspect_decision returned a JSON-serializable authoritative workspace at revision 7, READY, selected O1, 18 engineer-days, and zero provenance events.

The visible single-window synthetic-Jordan control used the real Jordan-authorized ordinary-UI mutation. The workspace advanced 7 to 8, capacity changed 18 to 14, state became CONTESTED, discovery changed 8 to 7 tools, and prepare_decision disappeared.

A cached revision-7 add_evidence call reached page code after Jordan's update and returned STALE_WORK_STATE with expected revision 7, actual revision 8, Jordan attribution, and the prescribed inspect/refetch/retry action.
Calling the removed prepare_decision handle was rejected by the native client before dispatch with: WebMCP tool registration is stale. Call fetchTools() again.
O1 selection exposed inspect_selected_option at epoch 2. Selecting O2 advanced to epoch 3; the cached O1 handle was rejected as stale, and refetched discovery inspected O2.

No ratify or commit tool appeared in READY, CONTESTED, REVIEW, or COMMITTED discovery. Native why_not reported that ratification is never available through WebMCP and Maya must act in the ordinary UI. The server-side rejection path is separately covered by D08 and D09.

After native recovery and preparation, Maya's visible UI action advanced revision 10 to 11 COMMITTED. Selecting customer-launch-brief advanced the page epoch to 4 and added inspect_followup with READY status and inherited context.

The judging client exposed fetchTools/call and delivered catalog-change notifications that required refetch. Its wrapper did not expose raw getTools or executeTool names, and callback cancellation-signal state was not directly observable on this surface.

The same deployment passed the ordinary two-window end-to-end flow with no WebMCP global in Playwright, five consecutive times. This is labeled automated fallback evidence, not native invocation evidence.
The complete native trajectory produced no page-console entries. The final production browser suite passed 7 of 7 checks, including the 390 CSS pixel smoke and reset rebinding regression.
